title: Lisbon vs Porto: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Porto for concentrated beauty and port wine in 3 days. Lisbon for variety, Sintra day trips, and a full week of sightseeing. Do both via the 2h45m train.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: Porto is ~15% cheaper. Porto €50–75/day vs Lisbon €60–90/day.

categories.name: City Aesthetics
categories.summary: Porto's Ribeira and Dom Luís bridge are arguably the most photogenic cityscape in Europe.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Sintra is one of Europe's best day trips. Lisbon also has Cascais and Setúbal.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Porto: francesinha and tasca value. Lisbon: Pastéis de Belém and broader variety.

categories.name: Port Wine
categories.summary: Porto is the home of port wine. Vila Nova de Gaia lodge tours are unmissable.

categories.name: Monuments
categories.summary: Jerónimos Monastery, Tower of Belém, Gulbenkian Museum.

categories.name: Weather
categories.summary: Lisbon is Europe's sunniest capital; Porto is greyer and rainier Nov–Mar.

categories.name: Fado Music
categories.summary: Alfama is the undisputed home of fado.

faq.question: Is Lisbon or Porto better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Lisbon for 5+ days; Porto for 3–4 days. Both are excellent — the train between them takes under 3 hours.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Lisbon or Porto?
faq.answer: Porto is roughly 10–20% cheaper across accommodation, food, and drinks.
